title: The steward's mistaken tally
summary: The girl Mòrag Ruadh finds her own small wax-board tally of the hall's candles does not agree with the steward Pàdraig mac Ìomhair's great ledger; he finds the fault his own, a tally-mark set down twice, and sets his sums before her eyes from that evening forward.

title: The seven houses name Mòrag Ruadh
summary: The seven houses of custody, meeting at the vein-house on the death of the old king, send word to Cathair dhearg within the month that the crown will go to the girl of Clann Raghnaill who keeps her own small tally beside the steward's; the custody-book gives four lines and no reason beyond her house and her blood.

title: The queen's own book bound
summary: Mòrag Ruadh has a vellum ledger bound within the month of her crowning, clasped in iron rather than silver at her own asking, and enters the cost of her own coronation feast on its first page, signed under her own name.

title: Tòmas clears the moss from Carragh Cnoc bheag
summary: The priest Tòmas mac Aonghais spends a month clearing moss from the obelisk above Cnoc bheag with wooden scrapers rather than iron, and finds, once the stone stands bare, letters cut deep and old that answer to no shape the schools' own tables keep.

title: The queen asks after the unread stone
summary: Hearing the report of the cleared obelisk read to her hall, Mòrag Ruadh enters the cost of Tòmas mac Aonghais's oil and vellum into her own book without comment, and asks only whether the priests mean to try the letters again; the answer she is given is that they do not know.

title: Ruairidh mac Neacail hangs the catch in the wind
summary: When Caol shean's salt runs out on the second day of its greatest catch, the shed-foreman Ruairidh mac Neacail hangs what cannot be salted on lines strung the length of the lower town's lanes rather than let it spoil on the strand.

title: Caol shean returns to salting
summary: The dried catch sells poorly against salted fish, fetching less at market than a middling salted season the year before; Caol shean lays in salt from that year for a catch half again the size of any it has yet taken.

title: The queen judges the thousandth year a measure and no more
summary: Asked by the seven houses whether the vein-house's thousandth year deserves a feast or a fast, Mòrag Ruadh judges between them: one burning on the quay the count began from, no more coal in it than an ordinary hearth burns of an evening.

title: The queen's journey to Seann Skell
summary: Mòrag Ruadh rides down to Seann Skell over roads already hard with the season's first frosts to stand at Cidhe an Diosail for the thousandth year's burning, a week's journey she makes to see the measure kept rather than take a scribe's report of it.

title: The queen's entry for the burning
summary: Where another ruler's book might have set down a verse for a thousand years made into one evening's fire, Mòrag Ruadh's own book gives the cost of the coal reckoned to the vein-house's weights, and beneath it five words: one handful, nothing more.

title: Birth of Beathag Fhionn
summary: Mòrag Ruadh's daughter is born at Cathair dhearg and named Beathag before the child is a day old; the queen's book holds one line for the day and the name, set apart from the ordinary sums in a hand less steady than usual.

title: The mill-race market opened above Muileann fhada
summary: The hill-lords of Baile ghorm set a single market at Cnoc bhàn above the long mill-race of Muileann fhada to gather the south-east's scattered trade in one place, its rare good the pearls no other market sells in whole parcels.

title: Sìne nic Ruairidh sells a season's pearls whole
summary: The shore-woman Sìne nic Ruairidh brings a whole season's gathering to the mill-race market's first opening rather than sell it a pearl or two at a time along the road, and a trader of Cathair mhòr pays her more for the lot than she has ever been offered piecemeal.

title: Oighrig nic Ailein fixes Baile ghorm's blue
summary: After ten years changing one thing at a time in her own mordant, the dyer Oighrig nic Ailein finds a mixing that holds Baile ghorm's blue fast through washing after washing; cloth of it is worn within the year at the vein-house's midwinter gathering.

title: Mòrag Ruadh crowned at nineteen
summary: Mòrag Ruadh is crowned at Cathair dhearg at nineteen, the youngest ruler the red hall has seen since Eilidh Bhàn, and keeps her own small tally beside the steward's from the first day.
